MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MARCH 2, 2026

1.  CALL TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Romanelli, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter, Yoo

Commissioners Absent:  Olson, Nicklas (excused)

City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Dev/Public Works Director
  Jessica Slawson, Assistant to the City Manager
  Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Director Naughton reported that no Planning Commission minutes were included on the
agenda. Staff further indicated that the February and March Planning Commission minutes
would be presented for consideration at the April Planning Commission meeting. By
consensus, the Planning Commission continued approval of the minutes to the April meeting.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD MITIGATION
  PLAN UPDATE

Jessica Slawson, Assistant to the City Manager, presented a report reviewing the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan, explaining its purpose,
regional collaboration among the Peninsula cities, and its role in maintaining eligibility for
state and federal emergency management funding. She noted that Rolling Hills Estates
served as the lead agency, the draft plan was available for public review, and following
adoption and approval of the plan, it will be forwarded to Cal OES and FEMA for formal
adoption/approval.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission receive and file this report and direct staff
to return with General Plan amendments at a future meeting.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI thanked Jessica for her comprehensive review and noted her
increased responsibilities in her position. He expressed appreciation for her continued
efforts.

 COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked whether the two special districts associated
with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes (RPV) had been included in prior hazard mitigation
plans or if this was their first inclusion. Assistant to the City Manager Slawson stated that this
was the first time the two special districts had been included in a mitigation plan. She
explained that while Rancho Palos Verdes and Rolling Hills Estates have participated
together in hazard mitigation cycles in the past, special districts may adopt a local hazard
mitigation plan separately if desired, and that the decision was made to include the two
special districts in this plan.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked whether the special districts are required to
have a mitigation plan. Assistant to the City Manager Slawson explained that a mitigation
plan is required if the districts are seeking grant funding, which they are.

COMMISSIONER REPP LOADSMAN referenced her involvement with the American Red
Cross and noted a current initiative to work with cities to improve emergency preparedness
information available on city websites. Additionally, she asked who administers or manages
the PVP Ready website that had been presented. Assistant to the City Manager Slawson
stated that Rolling Hills Estates staff serves as the lead agency for administering the website
and noted that it is a shared Palos Verdes Peninsula domain and she would be a point of
contact for the City of Rolling Hills Estates through its website, which administers the PVP
Ready site.

  COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
  to:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.
There being no objection, VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

B.  2025 HOUSING ELEMENT AND GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS

Community Development and Public Works Director Naughton presented the 2025 General
Plan Annual Progress Report, highlighting multi-jurisdictional hazard mitigation planning,
traffic safety improvements on Palos Verdes Drive North, park and equestrian facility
improvements, participation in the South Bay Regional Housing Trust, progress on the
George F. Canyon Nature Center, updates to the historic preservation ordinance, and City
energy and resiliency initiatives. Senior Planner Katrina Kawagoe presented the 2025
Housing Element Annual Progress Report, noting the City’s RHNA obligation of 191 units,
ministerial approval of seven ADU applications, issuance of five ADU permits, and 80
certificates of occupancy issued in 2025, including the La Sevilla mixed use project with three
deed restricted moderate income units, and the City’s third consecutive year of exemption
from SB 423 streamlining requirements.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission recommends to the City Council, that staff
be directed to submit their respective APRs to the Governor's Office of Land Use and Climate
Innovation and the California Department of Housing and Community Development by April
1, 2026.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the City appeared to be at or ahead of schedule in
implementing the General Plan and asked staff to confirm. Director Naughton concurred,
noting strong progress in housing production, while acknowledging ongoing challenges in
achieving deeper affordability. She reported that a project in the pipeline includes 44 very
low-income units under the State Density Bonus Program, which may be constructed in the
next housing cycle.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked whether staff anticipated any negative feedback from the
Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation or the California Department of
Housing and Community Development. Director Naughton responded that no issues were
anticipated and that agencies typically only contact the City regarding minor technical
corrections.

   COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to:

  PRESENT THE GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL
  REPORTS TO THE CITY COUNCIL.

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  APPLICATION NO. PA-240560; ADDRESS: 0 Encanto Drive (APN:7551-015-030 &
  7551-015-900), Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Salvador Gonzalez,
  California Water Service Company; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Grading Permit
  (G-240561) for the importation of earth materials greater than 20 cubic yards to widen
  the driveway apron and raise appropriate grade levels to accommodate the
  installation of a new temporary portable generator for the California Water Service
  Company; and a Variance (V-240562) to construct fencing and a sliding security gate
  within the front and side yard that would exceed the maximum allowable fence height.

Senior Planner Kawagoe presented the staff report for Planning Application No. PA-240560
regarding improvements to the Cal Water pump station located at 0 Encanto Drive. The
project includes minor grading, drainage improvements, driveway apron expansion,
installation of new gates, fencing realignment, replacement of existing chain-link fencing with
wrought iron fencing, and placement of a temporary emergency generator to ensure
continued water service during power outages. A variance is requested to allow increased
fence heights due to the site’s unique utility function. Staff found the project meets required
findings; one letter of opposition and two letters of support were received.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take public
testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt resolution number PA-
240560, approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
  to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

Andrew Enriquez, resident of 2 Encanto Drive, spoke in opposition unless conditions were
met. Mr. Enriquez stated he has lived at the property since 2015 and has worked with Cal
Water for several years regarding impacts from the adjacent facility. He explained that
removal of trees and vegetation beginning around 2017 significantly reduced privacy,
increased noise, and contributed to dust entering his property, including pool equipment. He
noted the existing approximately 5½ foot fence does not provide privacy given grade
differences between the properties.

Mr. Enriquez described drainage and flooding concerns due to site grading and stated Cal
Water has indicated those issues may be addressed. He expressed that the proposed fence
height of approximately 10 feet would improve privacy, though he had previously requested
a taller structure, to mitigate noise, dust, and visual impacts. Additionally, he also raised
concerns regarding delivery confusion at the shared driveway entrance and requested that
Cal Water install a clearly designated mailbox or improved signage.

Mr. Enriquez further discussed existing Southern California Edison transformers and power
poles located on his property, stating he could not locate any recorded easement and
requested relocation of the infrastructure onto Cal Water’s property. He noted operational
noise, proximity to his pool, and safety concerns. Concluding his request for coordination of
project sequencing, asking that fencing be installed prior to grading to provide dust, noise,
and privacy protection during construction.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked the applicant’s representative, Mr. Andrew Enriquez,
to clarify the nature of the privacy concerns and the level of daily activity at the Cal Water
  3

March 2, 2026
 facility. Mr. Enriquez responded that there is activity on the Cal Water property every day,
including landscaping crews, personnel accessing and checking equipment, and staff
responding to alarms or surges, sometimes during nighttime hours. He explained that he
maintains regular communication with site personnel and often serves as a point of contact
due to being home at varying hours. He further noted that unauthorized individuals have
occasionally breached fencing and accessed the Cal Water property from neighboring areas.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR confirmed that the testimony indicated consistent traffic in and
out of the site, not limited solely to occasional equipment access.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked Mr. Enriquez to explain the source of dust impacts, noting
that much of the Cal Water property appeared to be paved. Mr. Enriquez explained that while
portions of the site are asphalted, removal of trees and vegetation resulted in exposed dirt
areas. He stated that landscaping activities, particularly leaf-blowing, have historically
caused dirt and dust to be blown over the fence and into his yard and pool equipment. He
noted efforts to mitigate impacts by coordinating his own landscaping schedule after Cal
Water’s crews.

COMMISSIONER YOO questioned the location of existing electrical transformers. Mr.
Enriquez stated that multiple Southern California Edison power poles and transformers are
located on his property, occupying otherwise unusable space due to vegetation restrictions.
He explained that Edison conducts periodic spraying and partial tree trimming and that trees
previously fell toward his property. He stated his belief that no recorded easement exists for
the electrical infrastructure.

COMMISSIONER YOO confirmed that Mr. Enriquez had been aware of the power
infrastructure since purchasing the property, and Mr. Enriquez acknowledged that the
equipment was visible at the time of purchase. He stated that efforts to resolve the issue
through Edison, Cal Water, Metro Water, and City representatives have not resulted in a
clear resolution. Mr. Enriquez expressed concern about safety risks associated with aging
infrastructure located near residential use, particularly in relation to pool and backyard areas.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked Mr. Enriquez whether the concerns raised had been
previously shared with Cal Water representatives. Mr. Enriquez responded that he has had
ongoing discussions with Cal Water personnel over several years and that prior discussions
included taller fencing concepts, which were later reduced due to Municipal Code limitations.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked whether Mr. Enriquez had reviewed the proposed plans
prior to the meeting and whether there were outstanding issues that he felt were not
adequately addressed. Mr. Enriquez stated that he had seen the plans for the first time at
the meeting and that while he did not wish to delay or obstruct a project that could ultimately
benefit his family, he hoped to ensure that certain commitments would be followed through.
He stated a preference for resolving issues through cooperative discussions consistent with
the City’s small-community character.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI noted the importance of formal conditions and written
commitments, explaining that informal conversations with contractors may not ensure
implementation. He expressed concern about clarifying expectations regarding construction
sequencing, generator duration, electrical improvements, and coordination between Cal
Water and Southern California Edison. He stated that the concerns raised appeared
reasonable and warranted careful consideration.

Director Naughton clarified that the inclusion of the side-yard fence and related project
elements were a direct result of discussions with the adjacent property owner. She explained
that the fencing required additional approvals, including Public Utilities Commission
authorization, and that Cal Water also undertook a survey and relocation of an encroaching
fence, resulting in restoration of property to the owner at 2 Encanto Drive. She emphasized
that the primary purpose of the project was installation of a temporary, diesel-powered
  4
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 2, 2026
 emergency generator to ensure water service during power shutoffs and emergencies,
particularly during fire season.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about dust mitigation related to areas
previously landscaped and inquired whether additional measures such as ground cover or
landscaping could be implemented. She also asked whether the electrical infrastructure had
been disclosed during escrow. Mr. Enriquez responded that he was aware of the
infrastructure at the time of purchase but could not locate any recorded easement
documentation.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked staff whether signage identifying the site as Cal Water
property and clarifying delivery access could be installed. Director Naughton responded that
there is no City prohibition against such signage but noted that Cal Water would need to
consider any security implications.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI thanked Mr. Enriquez and invited Cal Water to speak. Renzo,
Production Superintendent for Cal Water, and Clyde Iruken, Capital Delivery Manager,
confirmed that site signage includes the property address and contact information. They
stated that most of the site is paved and that residual dust may occur near the shared
property line. Proposed grading, new asphalt, and installation of a berm are intended to
improve drainage and reduce dust over time. Additional landscaping is limited due to the
presence of a 51-inch water main along the property line.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about Cal Water pumping stations on the Peninsula
and asked about security measures at the Encanto station. Mr. Renzo responded that
approximately 28 stations exist, with two inactive due to landslides. Mr. Iruken confirmed that
the secured station on Crenshaw Boulevard is a Cal Water facility upgraded under the Palos
Verdes Pipeline Project. They confirmed that cameras are not included in the current project.
COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR encouraged Cal Water to consider additional security.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked whether Southern California Edison transformers at the
rear of the site could be relocated. Mr. Iruken explained that the transformers referenced are
not part of the proposed improvements but stated Cal Water would review available
information and coordinate with Edison as appropriate.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked about the temporary generator. Mr. Renzo stated the
generator would be installed only during periods of potential power shutoffs, permitted for a
maximum of six months per year, rented, diesel-fueled, and approximately 1,000 kW in
capacity. He explained the generator would allow additional pumps to operate to maintain
water supply and fire flow during emergencies.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI referenced a letter from the Montecillo HOA supporting the project
following meetings with Cal Water, based on assurances provided. Commissioners
discussed whether a formal agreement was necessary. COMMISSIONERS YOO AND
MEDAWAR cautioned against imposing formal documentation, while COMMISSIONER
REPP-LOADSMAN noted that the HOA letter documents commitments on the public record
and emphasized Cal Water’s responsibility to follow through, including construction-related
dust mitigation.

Mr. Renzo confirmed that fencing along the shared property line would be installed prior to
grading activities.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO
to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-240560, WITH THE CONDITIONS
  PLACED BY THE PLANNING DEPARTMENT.

Ayes:  Romanelli, Medawar, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:  None
Absent:  None
Abstain:  None

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved resolution number
PA240560, a resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
granting a grading permit for the importation of earth materials greater than 20 cubic yards
to widen the driveway apron and raise appropriate grade levels to accommodate the
installation of a new temporary portable generator for the California Water Service Company,
and a variance to construct fencing and a sliding security gate within the front and sides that
would exceed the maximum allowable fence height located at 0 Encanto Drive, APN 7551-
015030. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City
Council by its own motion may appeal this project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-260013; ADDRESS: 3554 Lariat Lane
  (APN:7548-011-017), Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Reiko Michlig,
  Reiko Architecture; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-260014) for an interior remodel and additions to an existing two-
  story, single-family residence that includes 474 SF of first story additions and a 570
  SF second story addition; and a Variance (V-260015) to exceed the required height
  to setback ratio in the west side yard.

Senior Planner Kawagoe presented Planning Application No. PA260013 for a two‑story
single‑family residence at 3554 Lariat Lane. The project proposes first‑ and second‑story
additions totaling approximately 1,044 square feet without increasing overall building height
and includes a request for a Variance due to the height‑to‑setback ratio. Staff stated the
project is compatible with the neighborhood, meets required findings, preserves existing
landscaping, and results in 19 percent lot coverage. One letter of opposition was received.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take public
testimony, discuss the issues, close the public hearing, and adopt resolution number
PA260013 approving the project.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked questions regarding the letters of support submitted with
the application. Specifically, whether the letters verified that the neighboring property owners
had reviewed the project plans in full and understood what they were approving, noting that
the document provided consisted of signatures and addresses only.

Senior Planner Kawagoe responded that two documents had been transmitted to the
property owners, including the signed letter and the complete set of project drawings. She
stated that the signatures indicated acknowledgment that the owners had reviewed and
approved the plans.

COMMISSIONER OLSON expressed concerns regarding narrow private drives on Lariat
Lane, limited turnaround space, and mature vegetation encroaching into the roadway, citing
emergency evacuation and fire access issues under the City’s Hazard Mitigation Plan.
Additional concerns included increased residential intensity, building massing, and limited
setback articulation associated with the proposed addition.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI acknowledged the concerns raised but noted that the
Commission is required to evaluate each project independently and within the limits of its

  6

 authority. It was stated that the subject property is of sufficient size to accommodate the
proposed square footage under the City’s development standards.

Discussion occurred regarding the private nature of Lariat Lane and responsibility for
vegetation maintenance. Commissioners noted that tree trimming on private streets is
generally the responsibility of property owners and that some residents choose to maintain
mature vegetation for privacy, despite long-term safety and insurance implications. Several
Commissioners commented favorably on the project design, noting that the addition was well
distributed across the site and avoided excessive vertical stacking. It was stated that the
proposal appeared to be a workable and well-designed addition compared to other projects
previously reviewed.
  COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
  to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO
  to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that while prior comments were appreciated, the
application must be evaluated independently under the applicable code provisions, and
broader community issues were not applicable to this specific request.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked staff whether they were satisfied with the applicant’s
presentation and the proposed project. Director Naughton confirmed that although another
planner worked most closely with the applicant, the project had been reviewed and staff
supported approval of the requested height–setback variance. She explained that the
variance request was intended to maintain architectural compatibility and avoid unnecessary
demolition to accommodate a modest addition. Director Naughton further noted that the
purpose of the height–setback ratio is to prevent structures from impacting neighboring
properties. In this case, the affected side yard abuts a private street, and staff was able to
make the required findings to support the variance.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked whether the property was located within a High
Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Director Naughton confirmed that it was not, referencing the
City’s current Fire Hazard Severity Map. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented
that the Fire Department conducts annual inspections and would require corrections if
access issues were identified.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR noted the presence of a pool on the property and inquired
whether it was included in the application. Director Naughton clarified that the pool was not
part of the current proposal and would require a separate building permit if pursued in the
future.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  OLSON to:

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-260013, SUBJECT TO THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

Ayes:  Romanelli, Medawar, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter, Yoo
Noes:  None
Absent:  None
Abstain:  None

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

NONE

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton reported that construction is underway at the Nature Center site.
Demolition of the existing building and parking lot was largely completed during the prior
week.

Director Naughton further reported that paleontological monitoring conducted during
demolition activities resulted in the discovery of fish fossils contained within a large on-site
boulder. The discovery was reported in the weekly memorandum to the City Council. The
boulder was determined to have no identifiable provenance, and staff was directed that it
may be relocated elsewhere on-site. The fossils were salvaged and will be incorporated into
the completed project as an interpretive landscape feature.

Director Naughton also acknowledged Code Enforcement Officer Stephanie McFadden,
noting that she will be participating in her first Los Angeles Marathon on Sunday, March 8.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 8:37 p.m. to the next regular Planning

Denise Jaramillo, Administrative Assistant  Jeff Romanelli, Vice Chair
